cards.title: Use QC on initial manufacturer orders
cards.claim: The speaker recommends using a QC agent the first time a manufacturer is used, and says QC can reference the tech pack, weigh and measure the product, and check Pantone color.
cards.action: For a first order with a manufacturer, arrange a QC agent to inspect the product; Alibaba's inbuilt QC function or SGS are named options.
applies_when: Using a manufacturer for the first time
Reviewing production quality against a tech pack
do_not_use_when: Treating this passage as proof that QC is required for every order
Assuming all QC providers perform identical checks or have identical costs
unknowns: Which checks apply to a specific product
Whether Alibaba QC or SGS is available for a given order
evidence_quotes: "a quality control agency will actually go to the factory they'll use your Tech pack again as a reference and they'll weigh the product they'll measure the product they'll do all kinds of things they'll check the panone color"
"I highly highly recommend that every single uh first time that you use a manufacturer even the second or third time that you're using a QC agent to go check the product"

"Alibaba is they have an inbuilt QC function where you can just say hey send a QC agent out to this order or you can use any of the other ones like SGS it's quite expensive and big but they do compliance as well"

cards.title: Build and assign ownership for a critical path
cards.claim: A critical path is described as defining each process step, sequencing tasks, estimating task duration, assigning dates, and monitoring progress; the speaker recommends one person monitor and own the process.
cards.action: Create a visible critical path that lists every process step in order, defines durations and dates, assigns roles, and sets overdue notifications.
applies_when: Planning a product launch or supplier-side production process
Managing dependencies such as sampling and shipping
do_not_use_when: Assuming a project-management tool itself guarantees on-time delivery
Giving suppliers edit access without considering the speaker's stated concern about manipulation
unknowns: Which project-management tool fits the team
Actual durations for each process step
evidence_quotes: "we Define every single step of the process"
"we're going to sequence all of these events in the correct order"
"then you're going to define the time it takes to do them"
"we can set dates to every single uh step of the process"
"one person kind of monitoring and owning this process each step of the way is really important so I highly recommend uh assigning roles as well"
"set up notifications when something blows out"

cards.title: Exclude out-of-stock days from a sales forecast period
cards.claim: The speaker says forecasting from a 30-day period that includes 15 out-of-stock days can understate demand; instead, use the 15 in-stock days and extrapolate.
cards.action: When selecting historical dates for a forecast, identify out-of-stock periods and use the in-stock sales period for extrapolation rather than treating stockouts as normal sales days.
applies_when: Forecasting future demand from recent sales
do_not_use_when: Assuming extrapolation from 15 in-stock days captures seasonality, promotions, or other demand changes
Using this as a universal forecasting method without validating the assumptions
unknowns: Whether sales while in stock were representative of normal demand
Effects of seasonality and growth on the forecast
evidence_quotes: "let's say you're kind of out of stock for half a month or then you're in stock for the rest of the 15 days I'll see people grab those 30 days and forecast out the next 90 days based on those numbers not not recognizing that they were extremely out of stock in those those 15 days"
"realistically it would have been a much more accurate Way by grabbing the 15 days that they were in in stock and extrapolating that out"
